Write a Risk Register to Disk

Source: R/risk_register_io.R
write_risk_register.Rd

Exports a risk register to a flat file so it can be shared, reviewed outside R, or re-imported later with read_risk_register(). All columns are written, including the computed rpn and risk_level, so the file is a faithful, human-readable snapshot. Those computed columns are not trusted on re-import: read_risk_register() rebuilds the register through create_risk_register(), recomputing the FMEA scores from the assessed probability, impact, and detectability. A write -> read cycle therefore reproduces an equivalent register.

Usage

write_risk_register(register, path)

Arguments

register

A risk_register from create_risk_register().

path

Output file path. A .xlsx extension writes an Excel workbook (requires the writexl package); any other extension writes CSV.

Value

path, invisibly.

See also

read_risk_register() for the inverse, create_risk_register().

Examples

rr <- create_risk_register(data.frame(
  risk_id       = c("R001", "R002"),
  description   = c("Missing vars", "Bad derivation"),
  probability   = c(4, 2),
  impact        = c(5, 3),
  detectability = c(2, 3)
))
path <- file.path(tempdir(), "risk_register.csv")
write_risk_register(rr, path)
read_risk_register(path)
#> ℹ Risk Register: 2 risk(s), 2 open
#> ℹ   Critical: 0, High: 1, Mean RPN: 29
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   risk_id description probability impact detectability category owner mitigation
#> * <chr>   <chr>             <dbl>  <dbl>         <dbl> <chr>    <chr> <chr>     
#> 1 R001    Missing va…           4      5             2 general  NA    NA        
#> 2 R002    Bad deriva…           2      3             3 general  NA    NA        
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: status <chr>, rpn <dbl>, risk_level <chr>
unlink(path)
